A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisionCoach. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original VisionCoach benchmark evaluations, component ablations, prompting experiments and attention analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds HCSTVG evaluation and further backbone, proxy-supervision and prompting experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2-3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same adaptive prompt selection, GSPO training, self-distillation, grounding rewards and prompt-free inference procedure. Added backbone and prompt variants are experimental conditions.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot HCSTVG evaluation requiring joint spatial and temporal grounding (Section 4.2, Table 5). Earlier training datasets and evaluation benchmarks remain; the new backbone and proxy-supervision studies reuse existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The V-STAR comparison in Table 2 adds VideoZoomer, Conan, Video-o3 and VideoChat-R1.5, none evaluated there in v1. The new HCSTVG comparison also includes GPT-5.4. This substantially expands the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include HCSTVG with m_vIoU and vIoU thresholds, a Qwen3-VL-8B backbone, selector retraining with Qwen3-generated proxy labels, inference with and without visual prompting, and prompt-pool variants. The threshold sweep adds a 10% condition. Original default settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds tests of backbone transfer, dependence on proprietary proxy supervision and whether VisionCoach still benefits from inference prompts. Appendix E.4 adds prompt-combination analysis, and Table 12 extends threshold sensitivity. Earlier reward, top-N and selector ablations are retained after relocation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Added tables retain point-estimate reporting; the unchanged four RL rollouts per input are not independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values remain, including V-STAR's 61.1 accuracy, 34.3 mAM and 47.5 mLGM. Added results include HCSTVG scores of 19.3 m_vIoU, 25.4 vIoU@0.3 and 6.1 vIoU@0.5, additional baseline rows, and the appendix controls. Qwen3-based results concern a new backbone rather than a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1-15 retain equivalent loss, reward, identity-matching, temporal-gating and evaluation definitions. No substantive mathematical derivation, assumption or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The framework, selector, grounding-reward and prompt-free inference contributions remain. However, v2 removes 'under comparable settings' from the abstract's state-of-the-art claim, making that claim less qualified. The shortened conclusion otherwise preserves the central claims.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion interprets small inference-prompt gains as evidence of internalization, Qwen3 experiments as backbone generality, and open-source proxy labels as reducing proprietary-supervision dependence. It also argues that prompt types are complementary. The existing annotation-dependence and predefined-prompt limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's direct code-repository and model-checkpoint links while retaining the project-page link. Core training hyperparameters, GPU configuration, selector LoRA details and prompt templates remain. The new appendix identifies the additional backbone and proxy-label configurations.

R1.justification: v2 adds distinct references for VideoZoomer, Conan and human-centric spatio-temporal grounding. The main related-work discussion and research positioning remain. Reference renumbering, duplicate consolidation and publication metadata updates do not introduce additional research.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites streamline the introduction, ablation discussion and conclusion. Threshold, top-N and reward-combination discussions move into the reorganized appendix, and references move after supplementary material. The main section sequence and most explanatory text remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a narrower LNCS-style layout with different typography, running headers and resized displays throughout. It adds the HCSTVG table and four appendix tables, regroups V-STAR baselines, and relocates existing ablation tables. The ten figures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new inference-prompt, proxy-supervision and backbone controls address previously untested aspects of internalization and portability, while HCSTVG and additional baselines broaden empirical support. These provide an incremental quality gain. Limited protocol detail and absent uncertainty estimates constrain the additions, while removal of direct artifact links and the abstract's comparability qualifier slightly weaken reporting.
